mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate indicates monetary easing, which can lead to increased borrowing and investment, thereby driving up S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 30% or more of the periods following a federal funds rate decline, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts reflects stronger consumer demand and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If housing starts increase but S&P 500 returns remain negative or flat, the hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate indicates labor market weakness, which can negatively impact consumer spending and S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If unemployment rises but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Increased industrial production suggests stronger economic output, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If industrial production growth does not correlate with positive S&P 500 returns, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth exceeds CPI inflation, real economic growth is positive, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate > CPIAUCSL inflation rate
failure_condition: If GDP growth outpaces inflation but S&P 500 returns are negative, the hypothesis is disproven.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 5% may indicate tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If the federal funds rate exceeds 5% but S&P 500 returns remain positive, the hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, increased real consumer spending (RSAFS) signals resilience, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS growth does not lead to positive S&P 500 returns during tightening, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When employment (PAYEMS) increases and unemployment (UNRATE) decreases, it indicates a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If employment rises and unemployment falls but S&P 500 returns are negative, the hypothesis is rejected.
